[2026-07-09 | AAPL | Overweight | +5.4% | +5.5% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: Constructive on AAPL, but do not deploy the trader's oversized market entry. Start with a moderate initial tranche of roughly 15-18% of full standard allocation at market (reference 316.22); the proposed 32% with a 14.22-point stop is ~1.44% portfolio heat, already breaching the stated 1% cap, and a 302 stop cannot govern a 296.9 entry. Reserve the rest for two adds, each with its own stop: a small breakout tranche only on a decisive close above 318.7 and 317.40 on expanding volume, and a pullback tranche only if 304.63 or the 296.9 confluence holds and turns - never a pre-authorized buy into a break. Cap total heat at ~1% including gap/slippage and treat a decisive close below 296.9 as thesis invalidation.

**Investment Thesis**: Direction is not the contested part; execution is. The conservative analyst concedes the operating record - H1 FY2026 revenue +16.1%, GM 48.6% (Q2 49.3%, +225bps), EPS +19.8%, FCF $78.28B (+63.5%), net cash ~$61.9B, EPS still +~20% despite a 25.3% buyback slowdown - confirming its case is an entry-price argument, not thesis deterioration. Trend structure corroborates: 316.22 above the 10-EMA (304.63), 50-SMA (296.88) and 200-SMA (272.15), 50 above 200 and rising, MACD 3.95 vs 1.21 with an expanding histogram, RSI 63.85, VWMA 292.83 rising. The deciding execution point is the neutral analyst's sizing/stop arithmetic, corroborated by the conservative and unrebutted by the aggressive: 32% at a 14.22-point stop is ~1.44% portfolio heat before slippage and exceeds the 1% cap, and a single 302 sell stop triggers on entry below it, so 296.9 invalidation was never the operative limit. Adopting the neutral repair - smaller ~15-18% first tranche, per-tranche stops beneath their own triggers, no pre-authorized buy at 296.9 into a break - fixes the plan without abandoning the thesis. I discount the aggressive's treatment of the $12.5B intangibles build as free upside (as plausibly an expensive acquisition with integration risk) and the conservative's reliance on the June 12.7% drop as scare value (it ended in the 261.8M-share capitulation/reversal footprint anchoring this leg); I also weight the repeated 5-day lesson from two prior AAPL Underweight calls (+7.4%, +8.3% raw) against standing aside on an intact uptrend. Missing valuation multiples, consensus/estimate revisions, sentiment/positioning and July 2-7 news mean this is an operating-plus-trend decision, not a valuation call - hence gradual Overweight rather than Buy. Change triggers: Q3 gross margin rolling over from 49.3% or China discount-driven share defense confirms -> Underweight; decisive close below the 296.9 confluence (breaking 50-SMA and Bollinger middle) -> cut to residual, next reference 200-SMA 272.15; failed breakout (tag 318.7+, close back below 317.40) -> hold base tranche, do not add.

**Price Target**: not provided

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months, re-underwritten at Q3 FY2026 earnings

REFLECTION:
The +5.5% five-day alpha versus SPY supports the directional Overweight call, though five days cannot validate a 3-6 month operating-and-trend thesis. It supports the trend-structure and prior-lesson components—intact moving-average stack and the cost of standing aside on AAPL uptrends—while leaving the Q3 gross-margin and China-share triggers untested. Lesson: when direction is uncontested and execution is the only dispute, deploy the repaired moderate tranche immediately rather than letting sizing debate delay exposure.

[2026-07-08 | AAPL | Overweight | +4.5% | +3.2% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: Stay constructive on AAPL but accumulate in tranches rather than chase the $315.20/$316.94/upper-Bollinger $315.56 ceiling at $313.39. Deploy only ~25–30% of the incremental add as a tactical starter now, reserve the bulk for a stabilized pullback into the 10-EMA $302.05 and then the 50-SMA $295.90 (that second add only on a confirmed reclaim of the 50-SMA, with its own wider stop), and complete toward the 125–150%-of-standard target only on a >50M-share close above $317.00 that holds the 315.20–316.94 band on retest. Cap exposure near ~125% of standard until the binary ~July 30 FQ3 print clears, with the starter risk defined at $291.90 (below the VWMA $292.05), and note that ATR of $8.35 means gap risk around earnings is real — hedge or trim the tactical tranche if you will not hold the print. Horizon 3–6 months.

**Investment Thesis**: Direction is not the contested issue in this debate; sequencing is. The aggressive analyst won the quality and trend argument and neither opponent seriously rebutted it: AAPL's Q2 FY2026 print showed revenue of $111.184B (+16.6%), gross margin 49.3% (+230bp), operating income +21.3%, EPS $2.01 (+21.8%), H1 free cash flow of $78.283B (+63.5%) and roughly $61.9B of net cash. The technical structure is equally clean — $313.39 above the 10-EMA $302.05, 50-SMA $295.90 and 200-SMA $271.80, MACD 2.96 versus a 0.53 signal with a +2.43 histogram, RSI 62.23 (recovered from 32.2, not overbought), VWMA $292.05 confirming the volume-weighted trend. That combination rules out Hold and certainly Sell/Underweight: the conservative analyst conceded the trend is bullish and the company high-quality, and his "no new capital at the ceiling" prescription would leave the book underexposed to a rising 200-SMA trend on a fortress balance sheet. I weight that objection down further because our own 2026-06-30 Underweight on AAPL was wrong by ~8.5% of five-day alpha precisely by letting a technically nearby level drive underexposure — this time the level in question ($315–317) is above the price, so the asymmetry argument cuts for, not against, having exposure.

The conservative and neutral analysts nonetheless landed a genuine, unrebutted hit on the aggressive/trader proposal: a single $291.90 stop copied across entries at $313.39, $302.05 and $295.90 is internally incoherent. It is ~2.6 ATR below the starter (defensible), but it is less than half an ATR below a $295.90 add, where normal noise with ATR $8.35 would clip it or force an undisclosed wider stop and larger real risk. The aggressive analyst never answered this, and his 40–50% starter at the ceiling also treats a 41.3M-share stall against a proven resistance shelf — below the plan's own >50M quality-breakout threshold, after a +13.9% two-week rip, three weeks before a binary ~July 30 print — as a sizing detail rather than a real discount. That is optimistic sizing, not discipline.

So I adopt the neutral analyst's framework with one adjustment. Neutral wins the debate because it correctly splits the difference: it preserves the aggressive's legitimate opportunity-cost point (a de minimis starter is not a chase, and a volume-backed break above $317 can gap away from the patient buyer) while importing the conservative's valid process demands (tranche-level stops, no full size into a binary event, no mechanical add at $295.90 with an inappropriate stop). My one adjustment runs in the starter's favor, on the AMZN lesson that the initial clip should be sized to fundamental conviction rather than shrunk purely on entry mechanics: a ~25–30% starter (between neutral's 20–25% and the aggressive's 40–50%) is proportionate for a company still expanding margins with $78B of H1 free cash flow.

The remaining forward evidence is genuinely mixed and is why this is Overweight rather than Buy, and why the ~125% cap holds until the print: UBS's ~3% App Store growth figure is a third-party Sensor Tower estimate, not company disclosure, but Services is central to the margin story; memory-cost pressure is a real bill-of-materials headwind dated after the record-margin quarter; the effective tax rate is up to 17.5% from 15.0%; buybacks fell ~25% to $37.0B; and the $12.5B jump in intangibles signals an unquantified acquisition with integration risk. Offsetting that, Broadcom's supply agreement through 2031, Luxshare's $3.1B IPO and the foldable "strong demand, limited supply" narrative are real medium-term supports. The packet contains no valuation multiple, no quantified memory-cost margin estimate, no updated forward guidance and no options pricing — that absence is why the tactical tranche should be explicitly earnings-aware rather than why we should abstain.

Rating changes: a >50M-share daily close above $317.00 that holds the 315.20–316.94 zone on retest, plus confirmed Services reacceleration in Apple's own disclosure or credible memory-cost relief, upgrades to Buy and the full 125–150% target. Conversely a high-volume breakdown through $296–291.90, gross margin rolling over on memory pass-through, confirmed App Store deceleration, or evidence the $12.5B intangible bet is not accretive moves AAPL to Hold and then Underweight.

**Price Target**: 340.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months

REFLECTION:
The +3.2% five-day alpha (+4.5% raw) validates the directional Overweight call, though five days is far too short to judge a 3–6 month thesis built around the ~July 30 print. The window supports the core quality-and-trend argument (price above the 10-EMA/50-SMA stack, no overbought RSI) and undercuts the conservative "no new capital at the ceiling" objection, but it also exposes the sequencing weakness: price never pulled back into $302.05/$295.90, so only the 25–30% starter participated. Lesson for next time: when direction is the high-conviction variable and the pullback zone is 3–4% below spot, size the starter larger or place a time-based second tranche rather than assume the dip arrives.

[2026-07-07 | AAPL | Hold | +1.4% | +0.8% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Hold

**Executive Summary**: Final decision for AAPL is **Hold**. Maintain existing AAPL exposure at roughly the caller’s standard-allocation weight; because no holdings or cash were provided, do not assume a flat book—if already overweight, trim back to plan, and if underweight, do not chase at market. Do not add AAPL at 310.66 into the 315.2–315.5 resistance zone. Conditional adds only: a smaller first breakout tranche after a decisive daily close above ~315.5 on volume ideally above the 75.4M 07-02 print and with follow-through or a successful retest/higher low; a pullback tranche only if the 299.5–295 zone stabilizes on a closing basis; reserve the final tranche for a held retest of ~295. A closing-basis break below ~295 trims toward defensive weight, with ~273.75 as the hard tactical exit line. Verify the $12.8B intangibles increase and obtain valuation/consensus data before increasing gross exposure.

**Investment Thesis**: The evidence supports AAPL **Hold** after weighing the debate, not because the analysts disagreed but because the stronger points split across time horizons. The aggressive analyst is right that AAPL’s medium-term setup is intact: price at 310.66 is above the 10 EMA at 299.53, the 50 SMA at 295.06, and the rising 200 SMA at 271.42; MACD has a fresh positive crossover with histogram +2.014; RSI is 60.66, not extended. Fundamentals also argue against trimming a standard position: Q2 revenue growth of 16.6% to $111.2B, gross margin 49.3%, operating margin 32.3%, EPS growth 21.8%, roughly $78.3B H1 free cash flow, and about $61.9B net cash.

The conservative and neutral analysts are stronger on immediate risk/reward. AAPL just rallied ~13.6% in seven sessions into the well-defined 315.2–315.5 shelf and was rejected on 07-07: opened 315.29, tagged 315.48, closed 310.66, with the upper Bollinger band near 313.39. Upside to the breakout trigger is only ~1.5%, while the 10 EMA is ~3.6% below, the 50 SMA/Bollinger mid/VWMA cluster around 295 is ~5% below, and the 273.75 June low is ~11–12% below if 295 fails. The 42.5M rejection-day volume versus the 75.4M 07-02 up-day is not convincing distribution, but it is also not proof of accumulation.

The forward unknowns are real but not yet decisive enough to force an Underweight on a standard position: UBS’s DDR contract forecast of +32% QoQ implies potential memory-cost lag; buybacks slowed to $37.0B H1 from $49.5B prior year; the tax rate rose to 17.5% from 15.0%; the $12.8B intangible jump is unexplained; and no valuation/consensus or social-sentiment data was provided. The conservative analyst’s proposed stop at 295 is too tight given ATR of 8.39—295 is roughly 1.9 ATR below 310.66 and could be pierced in a normal shakeout. The aggressive analyst’s automatic breakout add is too aggressive immediately after a failed resistance test and with valuation unverified. The neutral framework wins: hold core AAPL, do not chase, require confirmation for adds, and use a closing-basis invalidation below 295 rather than a mechanical 295 stop.

What would change the call: upgrade bias toward **Overweight** for AAPL on a decisive daily close above ~315.5 with volume above 75.4M and follow-through/retest, especially if the intangibles and valuation gaps are resolved cleanly. Downgrade bias toward **Underweight** on a decisive close below ~295, or on confirmation that memory-cost inflation, slower buybacks, and the higher tax rate are compressing margins/EPS. A break of the 273.75 June low is the hard line to exit remaining tactical AAPL exposure.

REFLECTION:
The +0.8% alpha (+1.4% raw) modestly favors the Hold call, but five days is too short to judge a thesis built around the 315.5 breakout and 295 invalidation—neither trigger was tested. The window undercuts the weight given to the 07-07 rejection at 315.2–315.5, since that failed test produced no follow-through selling and price stayed above the 10 EMA; the medium-term trend and fundamentals side of the thesis holds up better than the near-term risk/reward caution. Lesson: a single rejection print on sub-75M volume is weak evidence for withholding adds—next time, pre-commit to the confirmation trigger and let price, not the rejection candle, dictate the tranche.

[2026-07-06 | AAPL | Overweight | +1.5% | +1.8% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: Overweight AAPL, but earn the increment in tranches rather than taking the full 1.25x standard allocation at $312.66. Cap pre-Q3 exposure at roughly 1.125x standard (half of the 0.25x overweight increment): anchor one-third of the increment only on a pullback into the $294–$297 confluence (50-SMA $294.31 / 10-EMA $297.06 / Bollinger mid $294.87) with stabilization confirmed, and add a second, partial piece only after two consecutive daily closes above $317.40 on volume at least matching the 75.4M-share July 2 bar followed by a retest that holds. Stop the anchor on a daily close below the VWMA at $290.82, size on ATR $8.63 so a slide to the $275.15 June low is survivable, and hold the final tranche for the late-July Q3 print contingent on gross margin near/above 48.6%, a stabilized buyback pace versus the $37.0B H1 run-rate, and disclosure of the inferred ~$12.5B acquisition as non-dilutive/accretive.

**Investment Thesis**: The bull carried the half of the debate that determines whether AAPL is worth owning, and neither the conservative nor the neutral seat contested it. H1 FY2026 revenue rose 16.1% to $254.94B (Q2 +16.6%), diluted EPS +19.8%, gross margin 48.6% versus 47.0%, operating margin 34.0%, with R&D +32.6% YoY against SG&A +7.7% — genuine operating leverage with forward investment, not margin harvesting. The balance sheet is a shock absorber: ~$146.6B cash against ~$84.7B debt (~$62B net cash), ~$8B of debt retired, and ~$78B of H1 free cash flow on top of FY2023–FY2025 FCF of $99.6B / $108.8B / $98.8B and cash conversion of 1.15x. The bear's structural argument never got past entry timing: price $312.66 sits above the 10-EMA $297.06, the 50-SMA $294.31 and the 200-SMA $271.06, all rising, with the golden-cross regime intact, RSI 62.43, a fresh MACD bullish cross, VWMA $290.82 below price, and volume confirmation from the 261.8M-share June 26 capitulation and the 75.4M-share July 2 breakout. Nothing in that structure supports reducing exposure — it supports not paying up for it.

Where the conservative and neutral seats scored, and where I adopt their discipline: (1) the $312.66 entry is poor — pinned at the upper Bollinger Band $312.68 after a +13.6% seven-session run, directly beneath the $314.20/$315.45/$317.40 supply stack, with ATR expanded to $8.63 from ~$5.5, and three weeks ahead of a Q3 print whose bar was just raised by a record H1. (2) A single daily close above $317.40 is not sufficient confirmation in this tape; I require two consecutive closes on volume at least at the 75.4M-share July 2 bar plus a retest that holds, and if it gaps through, no chasing — wait for the retest. (3) The $290.82 anchor stop is only ~$4.68 (under 0.55 ATR) below the $295.50 entry, so share count must be cut and the tranche kept small, not run at full size. (4) FCF quality is overstated: the +53% operating cash flow headline is flattered by a ~$23B swing in other operating liabilities (+$7.3B this year vs −$15.6B last year), FY2025 FCF actually fell ~9% from FY2024, and the honest description is a stable ~$100B machine, not a surging one. The decisive asymmetry: the bear won points about the rate of change, the quality of one line item, and the entry price; it produced no evidence that the franchise is deteriorating.
